# ESP Web Tools 10.4.0, vendored

- **What:** the browser build (`dist/web/`) of [ESP Web Tools](https://github.com/esphome/esp-web-tools) 10.4.0, by ESPHome (the Open Home Foundation), Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`, from the package). The setup page flashes the pager with it (phase 5 design D5P-4).
- **From:** the npm package `esp-web-tools@10.4.0`, checked with valvur `check_package` (not flagged) on 2026-11-03 and again on 2026-11-07.
  - The registry's `shasum` (sha1): `594e2c7c06dced84bfc6dd1d0ee80e591867769f`
  - Its `integrity`: `sha512-3pwkeFFm5Fj7UQo8SJNYK5RXrtNCpq6X9QoI6bMT4GBZWgrJqjn0YvM9ihG74BtMoSFYXfmDtkehuxe50PTMPQ==`, which is sha512 `de9c24785166e458…d0f4cc3d` in hex; the tarball's own `shasum -a 512` matched it before anything was taken from it.
- **What's here:** `package/dist/web/*` unchanged, `package/LICENSE` and `package/package.json`. Nothing else from the package (its TypeScript sources, logos, screenshots or scripts).
- **What its browser build bundles:** its `package.json`'s dependencies, `lit`, `@material/web`, `esptool-js`, `improv-wifi-serial-sdk` and `tslib`, with theirs. That `package.json` is the package's own, kept for its version and licence fields: it isn't this project's manifest, and nothing installs from it. valvur `check_package` flagged none of them (2026-11-07). `THIRD_PARTY.md` lists ESP Web Tools and what it bundles.
- **`package-lock.json`, the runtime part of the release's lock file** (added 2026-11-07, open-items O-94): the browser build bundles the package's runtime dependencies at the versions its own lock resolved, but `package.json` names only ranges, so a scan couldn't check them (valvur: `inconclusive`). This file is `package-lock.json` from ESP Web Tools' tag `10.4.0` (commit `fab2ba48253d19fd29a15af57bec771d34978b62`), its `dependencies` the same as this `package.json`'s, with the 304 packages it marks `"dev": true` (the build tools, rollup, babel, typescript and the rest, which never reach the bundle) removed and its version set to 10.4.0. The 12 left are what the bundle carries: `lit` 3.3.3, `lit-element` 4.2.0, `lit-html` 3.3.0, `@lit/reactive-element` 2.1.0, `@lit-labs/ssr-dom-shim` 1.2.0, `@material/web` 2.4.1, `esptool-js` 0.6.0 (with `pako` 2.2.0 and `atob-lite` 2.0.0), `improv-wifi-serial-sdk` 2.8.0, `tslib` 2.8.1 and `@types/trusted-types` 2.0.7. valvur `check_package` cleared all 12, and a valvur scan of them found no vulnerability (2026-11-07). On an update, take the new tag's lock the same way.
- **Nothing is fetched at run time:** the page loads `install-button.js` from here, and it imports only its own chunks beside it. Its scripts name other sites only as links a person may follow (USB drivers, Home Assistant), never as something to load.
- **Under the page's CSP:** ESP Web Tools styles its elements through constructable style sheets, which `style-src 'self'` allows. Two static `style` attributes in `index-*.js` (the no-port-picked help's icon size and an SVG fill) are dropped, so that icon may draw at its natural size. No directive was added for them.
- **To update:** take a new version the same way, into a folder of its own name; change the `<script>` in `../../../index.html`, this repository's `THIRD_PARTY.md` and the licence texts in `tools/release/licenses/` (one per bundled package; `TestTheLicencesCoverTheSetupPagesBundle` names any missing), and the test's expectations if the chunk names it reads change.
